body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: 36fc8d663ad3bf5aa86737041379ea527bcd6764 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

Thanks for this one. Replacing the `UNJUDGED` name list with a marker that the guard checks against the judged set is the stricter design #1093 asked for, and the probes below confirm it.

### What looks good
- All five `arc_planes.nc` goldens differ from `origin/main` by exactly one added first line. With that line removed, each file is byte-identical to main (`cmp`; LF endings unchanged, no motion, word, order or whitespace change). The comment syntax fits each dialect: `(...)` for Fanuc, Haas and Mazak, `; ...` for Sinumerik and Heidenhain.
- The marker exists only in test code. Searching every `.rs`, `.cps` and `.nc` in the repo finds the string only in `crates/app/tests/common/mod.rs:257`, `heidenhain_block_form.rs:52` and the five goldens. No product crate or post script writes it, so a user's posted output never carries it. The golden test still compares the real post output byte-for-byte under the marker (`arc_planes.rs:149`).
- The guard is stricter: `posted_golden_verdict` (`solid_law_goldens.rs:304`) refuses a marked golden whose stem a gate judges, and refuses an unmarked golden that no gate judges. Its negative unit test covers both cases.
- `heidenhain_block_form.rs:49-54` only drops a leading marker line before the existing frame checks. No assertion was loosened.
- The reason is stated in the PR body and in `docs/decisions/1093-arc-planes-fixture.md`. `Changelog: none` fits a test-only change. No PNGs, no `CHANGELOG.md`, no process files, no new dependencies.

### Local results (trial-merged with `origin/main` 53a52f88, clean auto-merge)
| Suite (camcraft-app) | Result |
|---|---|
| arc_planes | 8 passed |
| solid_law_goldens | 6 passed |
| heidenhain_block_form | 5 passed |
| golden_cl | 26 passed |
| posting | 17 passed |
| fanuc_post | 12 passed |
| conformance | 6 passed |
| recorded_post_streams | 2 passed |
| clippy `-D warnings` on these 8 test targets | clean |

Guard probes, run locally on `every_posted_golden_is_a_program_the_gate_passes` and reverted afterwards (nothing pushed):
- A: `drill_plate.nc` (a judged program) copied with the marker into `nc/probe/`: **fails** with "carries the synthetic marker but a gate judges its op program".
- B: a new `probe_unjudged.cl` plus an unmarked `.nc`: **fails** with "posted, but no gate judges its program and it is not marked synthetic".
- D: the marker removed from `nc/arc_planes.nc`: **fails** the same way, so the `UNJUDGED` list is really gone.
- C (by design): a new unjudged stem with the marker passes. That is the escape hatch the issue intended. It now shows up in a diff as a marker line in the golden itself, not as one line in a name list.

### Requested before merge
None.

### Notes (not blocking)
1. The marker sits before the leading `%` (Fanuc family) and before `BEGIN PGM` (Heidenhain), not inside the program. This is harmless because only the golden carries it and no control ever receives it. It is also what lets the guard read it as "first line", as the issue asked. If a later test ever feeds a golden file straight to a control parser, it will need to strip the line the way `heidenhain_block_form` does.
2. `heidenhain_block_form.rs:52` repeats the marker text as a literal. Using `common::SYNTHETIC_MARKER` would keep the two from drifting apart, but the guard would catch a drift anyway, since `arc_planes` would then fail.
3. This existed before the PR: `every_posted_golden_is_a_program_the_gate_passes` skips any golden whose first line holds `REFUSED_HEADER` before judging it (`solid_law_goldens.rs:369`). No golden uses that header today. A follow-up could apply the same cross-check to it as this PR applies to the synthetic marker.
4. The PR body mentions a `coarse_laws` failure on wording. I did not run that suite because this diff does not touch it.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
